basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Describes a software product as a whole: business, design, implementation, runtime, risk, data and AI lifecycle, ownership and economics.
Organized in 13 bundles that an agent can read selectively, unlike a single architecture diagram.
Keeps the meaning of artifacts separate from the formats they are stored in.

may: Read AGENTS.md, the registry and the requested bundles before acting.
Add artifacts with stable IDs and canonical serial names.
Edit artifacts while preserving identity, provenance and history.
mustNot: Delete an artifact instead of deprecating it first.
Change a layer's meaning without a versioned migration.
Treat a missing artifact as permission to invent its content.
requiresHuman: Releases, architecture decisions and risk acceptance recorded in the model.
Changes to ownership and governance bundles.

considerations: Software built with AI agents affects its users; risk, compliance and data lifecycle bundles exist so that impact is recorded, not assumed.
Ownership records make it clear who answers for a decision an agent proposed.
affectedParties: People whose data the software processes

owners.steward: The product owner of each software system owns its AISMM instance; bundle stewards and layer owners hold delegated responsibility.

items: Product key and stable artifact IDs.
Bundle and layer IDs (for example 001 Product Definition and Context).

properties.reason: Software has no physical body; its runtime footprint is recorded in the operations bundles.

items: An AISMM workspace has AGENTS.md, a registry and bundle folders b0 to b12.
Read, add, edit and deprecate artifacts per bundle and layer.
Agents changing code without the context recorded in the model.
Software products built or operated with AI agents.

sections.whatItIs: A meta-model of a software product built or operated with AI agents: 13 bundles of layers, findings and questions covering product definition, business dynamics, system design, implementation, behaviour, user interaction, runtime operations, quality and compliance, change, knowledge traceability, data and AI lifecycle, ownership and governance, and technical economics.

relations.note: A product landscape (PLMM) federates the AISMM instances of its products.
World model of an AI system; AISMM describes the software product around it.
Datasets used and produced by the product are described by the dataset model.
